clue.text: A jolly old fellow's decisive battle

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
old means aged
a fellow of a university college is a don

explanation.surface: An elderly cheerful man takes part in a battle that settles everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective for the old fellow, but it is the slang noun for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the prophesied final conflict, hence any battle that decides everything.

clue.text: About to go off or come back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
milk that goes off is said to turn

explanation.surface: Ready to leave or else to return.
explanation.definitionFit: To return is to come back to a place.

clue.text: Calamity Jane's inclination to carry a hidden gun

indicators.note: to carry means one word holds another within it

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt
a concealed weapon is an arm

explanation.surface: The Wild West heroine tends to pack a concealed pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: Calamity Jane here is not the frontierswoman but a person always predicting calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamity Jane is a nickname for a doom-monger, one who spreads needless alarm.

clue.text: Write at length about king in exile

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to expatiate is to speak or write at great length
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Writing extensively about a monarch who has been banished.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate lives away from their homeland, as one in exile does.

clue.text: Cheats starting puzzles differently

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of the word for puzzles
differently says that opening letter is to be altered

parts.note: riddles are puzzles

explanation.surface: Someone cheats by tackling puzzles in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first letter of RIDDLES; the new D is not clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is to swindle, so diddles means cheats as a verb.

clue.text: Man in court's right to rise

indicators.note: to rise in a down entry means the letters read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A man in court entitled to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is a male first name, a crossword use of man.

clue.text: Lead followed by spies casing the French port in the Med

indicators.note: followed by sets the second piece after the first
casing means the outer pieces enclose another

parts.note: the van is the leading part, as in the vanguard
le is French for the
the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: Spies trail a leader around a French harbour on the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Spanish city and port on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: .Tortures Stalin carried out in East, terribly

indicators.note: terribly means the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Stalin's torture carried out in the East, horribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried out in' looks like a description of tortures being performed, but it signals one name sitting within the other before 'terribly' shuffles every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something kept out of reach.

clue.text: Mistakes are holding sailor back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole assembly in the opposite direction
holding means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: a tar is a traditional name for a sailor

explanation.surface: Errors are keeping a seaman from moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' builds ATARRE, and 'back' reads it the other way round; 'sailor' is the usual crossword tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing errors, a plural synonym for mistakes.

clue.text: Bound to be short of cash

explanation.definitionFit: Strapped means both fastened with straps and, informally, lacking money.

clue.text: Showing care and effort editing end of historical novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement
end of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone takes pains revising the ending of a period novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being edited but it is the anagram signal for EDITING plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent describes conscientious, painstaking work: showing care and effort.

clue.text: In the meantime, observe opponent

indicators.note: observe asks us to look inside the preceding words for a run of letters

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, keep an eye on your rival.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person against something, an opposer.

clue.text: Boy will win girl over, it's implied, completely

parts.note: Al is a short boy's name
the future sense of is going to win: to get
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A lad is bound to charm a girl round, it is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's implied' signals that AL is to get her is the implied sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means entirely or completely.

clue.text: Hector liar about using words extravagantly

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells Hector the liar off for overblown language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a verb (to bully) but its letters join those of LIAR as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetorical language is showy and grandiloquent, using words for effect.

clue.text: After landing, get char from here for free

definitions.text: After landing, get char from here
definitions.meaning: an angler removes a caught fish, a char, from the barb

explanation.definitionFit: Off the hook is an idiom for freed from difficulty; a landed fish is literally taken off it.

clue.text: Heartfelt in the extreme — real touching

indicators.note: in the extreme points to the end letter of the word before it

parts.note: real means actual

explanation.surface: Something deeply heartfelt and genuinely moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' reads as moving but is the definition in its literal sense of contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactual means relating to the sense of touch, so it fits touching as an adjective.

clue.text: Unions put up reward for robber

indicators.note: put up in a down entry turns the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: the TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the British federation of unions
a purse is a prize of money

explanation.surface: Trade unions offer a bounty for catching a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutpurse was an old-fashioned pickpocket or thief.

clue.text: Fights to get a few words in one's ear

indicators.note: in one's ear means as heard, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: a few words make a phrase

explanation.surface: Quarrels break out to whisper something to a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a phrase' heard sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrays are public brawls, a plural noun matching fights.

clue.text: Make contact with stores for carpet

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to reach is to get in touch
pro means for or in favour of, akin to with

explanation.surface: Get in touch with shops about a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb meaning reprimand, not a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to reprimand them, and to reproach is to rebuke.

clue.text: Magistrate, virtuous one, going — to church

parts.note: virtuous means just
I is the Roman numeral one
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A righteous magistrate sets off to church.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice, as in justice of the peace, is a magistrate.

clue.text: Was fired up about going after the ghost wandering outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters wrap around the other pieces
wandering means the letters stray into a new order
going after places the turned piece behind the preceding word
about tells us to turn the word round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was all worked up chasing a wandering ghost outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired up' looks like one phrase meaning excited, but 'fired' alone is the definition. 'about' gives PU; 'wandering' makes GOTSH, which 'outside' wraps round the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Got the push is an informal idiom for was dismissed from a job.

clue.text: Bad situation for graduate

definitions.meaning: as in things coming to a pretty ...
to succeed in an exam or course

explanation.definitionFit: A pass is a critical state of affairs, and to pass is to get through a qualification.

clue.text: It's hard to part with drug

parts.note: to sever is to separate
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Giving up drugs is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or difficult, so hard.

clue.text: Pope introduced to tense film director

indicators.note: introduced to means one piece is put into the other

parts.note: tense means taut
a pope is a small freshwater fish also called the ruff or ruffe

explanation.surface: The pontiff is presented to a nervous movie-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' is not the pontiff but a little perch-like fish, also known as the ruffe; 'introduced to' places it just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: François Truffaut was a leading French New Wave film director.

clue.text: Voices producing songs

definitions.meaning: as a verb, expresses or ... views

explanation.definitionFit: To air is to voice an opinion, and airs are also tunes.

clue.text: Pagan procrastinator's pidgin phrase

parts.note: the broken-English promise of someone putting a job off: me, perform it at a future time

explanation.surface: A heathen who keeps saying he'll get round to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I DO LATER, the putter-off's words.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, so is a heathen or pagan in the old sense.

clue.text: European capital's flower festival

indicators.note: capital here means the first letter, the capital letter, of the word

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A European city's floral festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city but means the initial letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring festival of the resurrection.

clue.text: One acting in appropriate way if he's taken badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone behaving properly when he is seized roughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' is the verb meaning steal, not the adjective meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak thief steals stealthily, so behaves in an appropriating manner.
